Only a few countries on this map are shaded the darkest purple, meaning women hold half the seats or more. Most of the world is still well short.

a thread 🧵🗺️
1/ The map shows the share of seats held by women in the lower or single chamber of national legislatures, 2024. Data: Our World in Data (CC BY).
2/ Globally, women hold just over a quarter of national parliamentary seats, roughly 27%, up from about 24% in 2019. Progress is real, but it's slow.
3/ Rwanda has topped the world rankings for years, with more than 60% women in its lower house at the last count cited on Wikipedia. Mexico shows up in the darkest shade here too.
4/ The Nordics sit close to parity. Sweden was near 47% and Finland near 46% in the 2020 figures, and both look deep purple on the map.
5/ Nigeria, Africa's most populous country, sits in the lightest shades: 15 of 356 House seats and 7 of 107 Senate seats are held by women, about 4% and 7%.
6/ A pattern worth noticing: wealth doesn't predict the colour. Several middle-income countries beat much richer ones, and electoral rules and quotas often matter more.
7/ Why do you think the gap is so uneven? Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
